headline: TP-Link seeks to manufacture Wi-Fi routers in the US
summary: TP-Link proposed a $1 billion US manufacturing alliance with Key Tronic, as it tries to win FCC approval and appease the Trump administration after its new Wi-Fi 8 routers were blocked from US sale.

claims.statement: TP-Link proposed a $1 billion alliance with Key Tronic to manufacture Wi-Fi routers in the US.

sources.quote: TP-Link proposes $1 billion US Wi-Fi router manufacturing alliance with Key Tronic

claims.statement: TP-Link cannot currently sell its newest Wi-Fi 8 routers in the US, unlike rivals that have won FCC approval.

sources.quote: TP-Link can't sell latest routers in US despite rivals getting FCC approvals.
TP-Link, one of the world's leading manufacturers of consumer Wi-Fi routers, is in a precarious position in the US.

claims.statement: The move is widely seen as an attempt to appease the Trump administration over its foreign router ban.

sources.quote: TP-Link tries to appease Trump admin with pledge to assemble routers in US
can't bring them here because of President Donald Trump's foreign router ban.

discrepancies.explanation: Tom's Hardware frames the Key Tronic deal as a proposed alliance, while Ars Technica frames TP-Link's move as a firmer pledge to assemble routers domestically.
